title: Reasoning Evaluation & Calibration
description: Study benchmark contamination, pass-at-k and comparison fairness, calibration and abstention, and error taxonomy and reproducibility. Each lesson includes a worked example and an applied practice task.

lessons.title: Benchmark contamination
lessons.description: Describe how semantic overlap can inflate apparent reasoning ability.
lessons.conceptOverview: Evaluation data may overlap training or tuning material. Track provenance and use fresh or controlled tasks where possible; exact duplicates are only one form of leakage.
lessons.whyItMatters: Contamination includes near-duplicates and exposed solutions.

lessons.title: Pass-at-k and comparison fairness
lessons.conceptOverview: Pass-at-k describes whether at least one of k attempts succeeds under an evaluation protocol. Compare systems with matched sampling budgets and report single-attempt behavior separately when relevant.
lessons.whyItMatters: Attempt budgets are part of the metric's meaning.
lessons.engineerDeepDive: Pass-at-k describes whether at least one of k attempts succeeds under an evaluation protocol. Compare systems with matched sampling budgets and report single-attempt behavior separately when relevant.

sections.title: Concept
sections.content: Pass-at-k describes whether at least one of k attempts succeeds under an evaluation protocol. Compare systems with matched sampling budgets and report single-attempt behavior separately when relevant.

sections.title: Worked example
sections.content: One system gets one attempt and another gets twenty, then their success rates are compared without qualification.

sections.title: Practice & verification
sections.content: Design a fair budget-matched comparison. Write down your reasoning and check it against the concept before continuing.

keyTakeaways: Attempt budgets are part of the metric's meaning.
commonMistakes: Success rates are directly comparable regardless of attempt count.

lessons.title: Calibration and abstention
lessons.description: Explain the calibration gap and propose an abstention evaluation.
lessons.conceptOverview: Calibration compares confidence with observed correctness across groups of predictions. Use held-out data and allow abstention when uncertainty exceeds the task's tolerance.
lessons.whyItMatters: Confidence should be assessed against empirical correctness.

lessons.title: Error taxonomy and reproducibility
lessons.description: Define a run manifest and categorize a sample of failures.
lessons.conceptOverview: Classify failures by representation, calculation, evidence, tool use and verification. Record inputs, versions and budgets so improvements target causes and comparisons can be repeated.
lessons.whyItMatters: Reproducibility requires recording more than final scores.
